name: banana
sowing_season: Tissue culture plants: June–July (Maharashtra, Gujarat) or October–November; avoid planting in peak summer or winter
harvest_season: 11–13 months after planting (Grand Naine); the ratoon crop 8–10 months after the main harvest
soil: Deep, well-drained loam rich in organic matter, pH 6.5–7.5; banana cannot stand waterlogging

stages.name: Planting / Establishment
stages.description: Tissue culture plants or suckers settle in and grow new roots.
stages.irrigation: Irrigate right after planting, then keep the soil moist — by drip about 4–6 litres per plant a day.
stages.fertilizer: In each pit at planting: 10 kg well-rotted FYM + 250 g neem cake + 100 g DAP.
watch_for: Bunchy top virus in suckers — narrow, bunched leaves with dark green streaks
tips: Plant virus-tested tissue culture plants or healthy sword suckers

stages.name: Early Vegetative
stages.description: New leaves come every week and the stem thickens.
stages.irrigation: Drip 8–10 litres per plant a day in summer, less in winter.
stages.fertilizer: Every month: 50 g urea + 50 g MOP per plant around the plant, then irrigate (or give it through drip).
watch_for: Leaf spot (Sigatoka) starting on the lower leaves

stages.name: Vegetative Growth
stages.description: Fast growth of leaves and stem; the bunch starts forming inside.
stages.irrigation: Drip 10–15 litres per plant a day in summer; never let the plant wilt.
stages.fertilizer: Every month: 60 g urea + 80 g MOP per plant.
watch_for: Sigatoka leaf spot — yellow streaks becoming brown spots
Pseudostem weevil — jelly-like ooze and holes in the stem
Panama wilt — older leaves yellow and hang, the stem splits
tips: Cut off dry and spotted leaves and burn them

stages.name: Shooting / Flowering
stages.description: The flower bud comes out and the hands of fruit open.
stages.irrigation: The most critical time for water — drip 15–20 litres per plant a day in summer.
stages.fertilizer: Last urea dose: 50 g urea + 80 g MOP per plant at shooting.
watch_for: Plants falling over under the bunch weight
tips: Remove the male bud 1–2 weeks after the last hand opens
Prop the plant with bamboo poles
Cover the bunch with a polythene sleeve after the last hand opens

stages.name: Bunch Development
stages.irrigation: Keep it regular — water stress gives small fingers.
stages.fertilizer: 50 g MOP per plant once; no urea.
tips: Remove the last one or two small hands for bigger fingers on the rest

stages.name: Harvest
stages.irrigation: Reduce irrigation a week before harvest.
tips: For far markets, harvest when the finger ridges are just rounded (75–80% mature)
Keep one healthy follower sucker for the ratoon crop

common_pests.name: Rhizome weevil
common_pests.symptoms: Tunnels in the corm; plants weaken and topple
common_pests.control: Plant clean suckers; set split-stem traps and destroy the weevils collected

common_pests.name: Pseudostem weevil
common_pests.symptoms: Jelly-like ooze and holes on the stem; the plant breaks
common_pests.control: Remove and destroy affected plants; cut harvested stems into pieces

common_pests.name: Banana aphid
common_pests.symptoms: Dark aphids at the leaf bases; spreads bunchy top
common_pests.control: Destroy bunchy top plants together with the aphids; plant virus-free tissue culture plants

common_diseases.name: Sigatoka leaf spot
common_diseases.symptoms: Yellow streaks turning into brown spots with grey centres; leaves dry early
common_diseases.control: Remove spotted leaves; spray Propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml/litre with 10 ml mineral oil per litre

common_diseases.name: Panama wilt
common_diseases.symptoms: Older leaves yellow from the edges and hang down; the stem splits at the base, brown inside
common_diseases.control: No cure — uproot and destroy; do not replant banana there for some years; use resistant varieties

common_diseases.name: Bunchy top virus
common_diseases.symptoms: Narrow, upright leaves bunched at the top with dark green streaks
common_diseases.control: No cure — kill the aphids and uproot the plant; plant virus-free tissue culture plants
